purpose: Structured, provenance-preserving ingestion pack for Tupiniquim AI Toolbox. External sources remain untrusted references until a project-specific gate adopts them.

knowledge_units.content: Readiness and startup waits should be bounded. A request must receive an explicit unavailable/starting result instead of waiting indefinitely. Provider/model/harness identities remain separate concepts.
Credential validation should be non-generating and separate from inference. Diagnostics should redact secrets and avoid leaking provider credentials.
FCC automatic provider/model fallback is useful as a reference but conflicts with the current Tupiniquim rule that provider/model selection stays explicit and user-controlled.
Keep planning, agent state, tool collection, MCP transport and sandbox lifecycle as separable layers. Tools are capabilities, not authority.

Bash, editor, browser and external MCP tools must not be imported with upstream trust assumptions. Route privileged effects through PolicyEngine, allowlists, AuditLog, approval and workspace boundaries.

When humanizing prose, preserve supported claims, never invent facts or citations, match an explicit user writing sample when provided, and in file mode preserve code/data/frontmatter/commands/paths/link targets.

Use layered abuse controls: rate limits/quotas, API gateway or reverse proxy, WAF/CDN where appropriate, request and concurrency bounds, backpressure and observability. Application rate limiting alone is not volumetric DDoS mitigation.

A deterministic, non-secret canary invariant can act as an early warning for session/context drift or hallucinated continuity. It is diagnostic evidence only, not proof that all context is intact and not a security control.

Model authentication by factor and threat model: knowledge, possession and inherence. Password+PIN is not MFA because both are knowledge factors. Prefer MFA for privileged accounts and safe recovery/re-authentication flows.

Educational algorithm lists are not selection policy. Do not design custom crypto; prefer modern authenticated encryption and managed keys. 3DES/TDEA is legacy and not for new protection. Passwords use password hashing, not reversible encryption.

Use internal, external, physical, human error, supply-chain, credential, network, application, cloud and IoT categories as prompts for threat modeling, then convert them into assets, actors, trust boundaries, abuse cases and tests.
Hat/color and actor labels are informal awareness vocabulary. They must never grant authorization or determine pentest scope. Written authorization and target scope control offensive-security work.

rejected_or_deferred: Marketing/support CTA image: no reusable technical knowledge.
Automatic provider/model fallback: deferred because it conflicts with current explicit-selection policy.
Upstream unrestricted Bash/editor/browser execution: rejected without Tupiniquim policy boundaries.
Educational crypto algorithm list as implementation policy: rejected; authoritative standards take precedence.
Hacker-hat taxonomy as authorization model: rejected.
